edits.rationale: The Foursquare post-mortem (posted Oct 7, 2010) describes one shard outgrowing its RAM, slow queries causing a backlog, a third shard added, and fragmentation meaning that moving 5% of the data did not cut RAM need. MongoDB's 3.2 compatibility notes say WiredTiger became the default in 3.2, so the incident predates it. The 'treat as historical context' advice is the pack's editorial guidance, not a factual assertion.

edits.old: Queries without a usable shard key can require broadcasting to every shard and merging results. A plan to shard for throughput should assess how common queries will target shards; scattered requests can increase cost rather than provide proportional scaling. (high confidence)
edits.new: Queries without a usable shard key can require broadcasting to every shard and merging results. Such scatter/gather queries can be long running, and targeted operations are generally more efficient than broadcasts, so a plan to shard for throughput should assess how common queries will target shards. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/sharding.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharded-cluster-query-router.md

edits.old: Begin sharding design before the cluster reaches its capacity ceiling. Distributing existing data is resource intensive, and Percona warns that late chunk migration can interfere with production workload; allow operational headroom for the transition. (high confidence)
edits.new: Begin sharding design before the cluster reaches its capacity ceiling. MongoDB notes that distributing existing data after sharding a collection is slow and resource intensive, and Percona advises planning a sharding strategy early and running the balancer in low-traffic windows because its migrations can compete with the application's regular workload. Allow operational headroom for the transition. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/sharding.md ; https://www.percona.com/blog/mongodb-sharding-replication-101-the-communitys-questions-answered/ ; https://www.percona.com/blog/2017/10/16/when-should-i-enable-mongodb-sharding/

edits.old: No universal gigabyte cutoff justifies sharding. Percona explicitly rejects a hard size threshold; its separate 200–500 GB and 1–2 TB suggestions are planning heuristics, while MongoDB describes resource and throughput limits. (high confidence)
edits.new: No universal gigabyte cutoff justifies sharding. Percona says there is no hard number in gigabytes, though it suggests engaging around 200GB for backup/restore reasons and, in a Q&A, says some people cite 1-2TB but that may be too large and sharding strategies should be considered in the 200GB-500GB range. MongoDB describes large data sets and high throughput challenging a single server's capacity. Sources: https://www.percona.com/blog/2017/10/16/when-should-i-enable-mongodb-sharding/ ; https://www.percona.com/blog/mongodb-sharding-replication-101-the-communitys-questions-answered/ ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/sharding.md

edits.old: Working-set pressure is a more useful memory trigger than total database size alone. MongoDB identifies working sets larger than RAM as an I/O stressor; Percona distinguishes hot working data from rarely accessed historical data. (high confidence)
